HFIR Campaign Build. ....................................................................................... 3-40 UNCLASSIFIED AMMT – 316H SS Los Alamos National Laboratory Page iv Executive Summary In FY24, Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) collaborated with Argonne National Laboratory (ANL) and Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) to develop a machine-agnostic process parameter development and maintenance plan for additive manufacturing (AM) of 316H stainless steel. This effort aimed to increase the manufacturing readiness level of AM parts and systems. The team generated statistically relevant data sets of critical design properties and associated behaviors, providing manufacturing windows for use by the DOE complex. Building on FY23 research, this study emphasized the importance of material readiness independent of machine type, enabling rapid qualification and certification of AM parts and systems. The LANL team conducted a comprehensive investigation to determine the necessary machine maintenance plan and its relationship with processing parameters, mechanical behavior, and size effects. The study also explored non-destructive evaluations, the impact of surface finish on fatigue life, and the effects of electro-polishing and various post-processing techniques on fatigue life. Additionally, the team established the Peregrine code (developed by ORNL) and developed machine learning (ML) models to support these efforts. Objective Currently, the ASME Code has only approved six materials for nuclear construction at elevated temperatures, underscoring the need for a more efficient material qualification process.
